name: Testosterone

lead: Testosterone is the principal male sex hormone, an androgen produced mainly in the testes. It drives male secondary sexual characteristics, bone density, red blood cell production and muscle mass.

In medicine it is prescribed to treat diagnosed hypogonadism. Healthy young men given supraphysiologic doses gain muscle in a dose-dependent way, which is why anabolic steroid use is a feature of physique culture. Benefit is strong where there is true deficiency; use beyond that carries serious risks.

paras: Testosterone binds the androgen receptor, increasing muscle protein synthesis, satellite cell activity and bone formation, and is partly converted to estradiol and dihydrotestosterone with their own effects.

It is a prescription-only, controlled substance in many countries. Risks include suppression of natural production and fertility, acne, polycythemia, blood pressure and lipid changes, mood effects and possible cardiovascular strain; abrupt cessation can leave a deficiency. This entry is informational and not guidance for use.
